translations.title: They Call Him King and Blindfold His Eyes
translations.text:
They call him king and blindfold his eyes, and expect him to divine and not see; they give him a scepter swayed by wind, a crown of reeds and thorns.


With such ceremonies and spoils Judea's realm desires its king: let him command with a cane, possess pain, and blindly suffer its rage.


But the Lord, whose just rule is enclosed in a well-armed iron rod, reveals crowned mercy in his love.


He buys peace for his people with his war, spends the points and sword upon himself; learn from Him, you who govern the earth.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The Brief Year Carries Everything Away
translations.text:
The brief year of mortal life carries everything away, mocking brave steel and cold marble, whose hardness dares resist Time.


Before the foot knows how to walk, it moves toward death, where I send my obscure life: a poor, turbid river drunk by a black sea with towering waves.


Every short moment is a long step I unwillingly take on that journey, for standing still and sleeping, I always hurry on.


Death is a brief, final, bitter sigh, compulsory and inherited; but if it is law and not punishment, why do I grieve?
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The Same
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: These Are and Shall Be the Last...
translations.text:
These are and shall be the last tears that, with a living voice's force, I lose in this fugitive fountain carrying them to so many beasts' thirst.


Happy am I if on foreign shores, feeding such elusive grief, I find merciful death, which topples this vain architecture of chimeras!


A naked spirit, pure lover, I shall burn above the sun, and the cold body will remember Love in dust and earth.


I shall be my own epitaph to the traveler, for my lifeless face will say: “It once was Love's glory to wage war on me.”
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Prisoner in Love's Labyrinths
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Petrarch Celebrated His Fair Laura
translations.text:
Petrarch celebrated his fair Laura with genius and lofty style, and made his care eternal to the world, and the rare beauty he saw in her.


Many live envious of her, for so high a good and fortunate state, against which time can do nothing, deserves great envy.


I alone would wish to leave you, gallant, beautiful Silvia, to whom I gave my heart in sacrifice, the same good fortune.


For this soul, happy in adoring you, can render only this service: that neither time nor death offend you.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: If He Who Paints You Must See You
translations.text:
If he who must paint you must see you, and cannot look without going blind, who can portray you without offending his sight and you?


I wished to make you bloom in snow and roses; but that would honor roses and wrong you; I wished to give you two stars for eyes, but when did stars dream of that?


I knew the impossible in the sketch; but your mirror, by your own radiance, assured success in its reflection.


It can portray you without borrowed light, since in the mirror you are original, painter, brush, and copy.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To Aminta, That She Imitate the Sun and Leave Comfort When She Departs
translations.text:
Since you are the sun, learn how to depart from the sun that learns light and joy from you; did you not see day die yesterday and quench its burning gold in the sea?


Then the air, asleep in cold shadow, grew black and sorrowful; then night lit as many consolations in the East as lights had burned.


Aminta, you rise for Silvio from the sunset in which you leave me buried and blind; darkened, I follow with uncertain step.


Grant my night and plea, from your sun's fire in which I burn, stars—the castoffs of your fire.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: This Fountain Speaks to Me, but I Do Not Understand
translations.text:
This fountain speaks, but I do not understand its language; I know it speaks of love and boasts of seeing me burn for Flori against its will.


I understand my weeping, by which it grows, for it proclaims my grief; my tears crown the meadow; the crystal goes laughing away with them.


My heart owes little to my eyes, for they give water to water and deny it to the fire consuming me.


If they do not see because weeping blinds them, let them hear what they cannot see: they leave me burning and drown the water itself.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: A Thousand Deceitful Phantoms Surround Him
translations.text:
What image of harsh death, what shadow of hell torments me? What cruel tyrant follows and kills me with vengeful, lawless hand?


What phantom in the fearful night tears my heart from sleep? Who avenges you on me, divine ingrate, beautiful more for my harm than your good?


Who, when with doubtful foot I tread this sand's solitude, fills the desert with my cares?


Who returns my chain's ancient sound to my ears, if it is certain you do not even remember to cause me pain?
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: If the Madman Never Had Hope
translations.text:
If the madman never had hope, nor the wise man despair, from what accidents do I lose my life today? What feeling reaches my reason?


Who changes my memory so I forget what I seek? I see it dreaming, and wake without sleeping: evil weighs and good balances equally.


I listen deaf and recognize blind; rest working and speak mute; humbly wait and proudly ask.


If this unrest is not love, I doubt I can know what ends me: no one lives more surrendered to himself.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To an Adulteress
translations.text:
In you alone, Lesbia, adultery has lost its shame before heaven, since openly and unveiled you have offended noble bones.


By God, you, me, and your husband, do not let earth know your infamy: close the door; sin was born to hide.


I do not say leave your friends, but they should not be noticed by your few enemies.


Your affronted neighbors say the witnesses to your sins delight you more than the sins.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: His Homeland Could Fail Great Osuna...
translations.text:
His homeland could fail great Osuna, but his deeds not its defense; the Spains gave death and prison to him who made fortune their slave.


His envies wept; foreign nations with his own: Flanders' fields are his tomb, the bloody moon his epitaph.


At his funeral Parthenope lit Vesuvius, Trinacria Mongibello; martial weeping swelled to flood.


Mars gave him heaven's best place; Meuse, Rhine, Tagus, and Danube murmur grief.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Definition of Love
translations.text:
Beg her? Be scorned? Love her? Follow her? Defend herself? Seize her? Grow angry? Desire and not desire? Let herself be touched, then resist persuasion?


Hold her? Try to break away? Wrestle in her arms? Kiss her unwilling, have her take offense? Fail to leave?


Have her insult me, reprove my pleasure, then abandon her frown and show no displeasure?


Consent to moving her shift, find it clean and fit it neatly? This is love; all else is laughter.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Don Francisco de Quevedo
translations.text:
I am stone in suffering pain, wax in tender love; wise in loving noble pain, foolish in persisting in my harm.


Fearful of not defeating my cowardice, brave in not being defeated by myself; human feeling hurt, beast not awakening disabused.


Among red fires, amid your harsh cold disdain, I am a salamander fulfilling your whims;


and my pupils, with your eyes absent, became nymphs dwelling within two rivers.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Weeping, I Enraged the Current
translations.text:
Weeping, I enraged this fertile crystal river; singing calmed its course: so much can grief do in one absent!


I saw myself in the fountain before cold ice seized it, and saw my face deserves your burning light.


I left its waters rich with spoils; Isbela, it covered your altars with incense and grain.


I dried and swelled Henares with water and fire; in one stream I saw two seas in my eyes.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To Belisarius
translations.text:
Seeing you triumph beyond the moon over barbarous foes, who would not fear, noble Belisarius, that you made Fortune envious?


These sad tears I owe your extraordinary valor, which hid commanding Marius in oblivion.


Now among beggars, time tyrannizes you, and memory of highest spoils.


Your enemies wished to blind you, not seeing he cannot be blind who has so many eyes in fame.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: That August Brow Which Crowns
translations.text:
That august brow crowns all sea surrounds and sun shelters; what he does not govern, God punishes by not subjecting it to him.


Clothing Flora and Pomona, he commanded time to follow his colors and winter deny its ice.


He sent west the envious sun that turned December to May, its light frowning and gold faint.


He ran gallantly and struck bravely; cane became arrow and lightning; Lope alone could sing him.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: By Winter's Example, He Imagines Whether Lisi's Ice Will Admit His Fire
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To the Sea
translations.text:
You wear God's will as shackles, and law written in sand humbles you; to kiss it you reach shore, obedient sea, driven by surges.


You halt within your pride, humble enough to resist it; your prison amazes you, rich to our harm with our goods.


Who gave pine and beech daring to occupy fishes' dwelling, and linen to obstruct wind?


Surely seeing you captive: greed for pallid gold, God's wrath directed against man.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To King Philip III
translations.text:
Hidden beneath your fleet the sea groans, sail calls wind, and heaven promises the Turk's crescents eclipse on your campaign.


Your sword wishes in English veins to quench Spanish thirst, while the sun sees his brightness increased in your arms.


Perhaps envious earth arms triumphant armies against you, powerful in proud monsters;


seeing your right hand armed with lightning, O Jupiter, I think giants returned to the world.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: My Eyes Strengthened the Current...
translations.text:
My eyes strengthened this gentle river's current; singing checked its course: so much can grief do in one absent!


I saw myself aflame in this fountain before ice seized it, and saw my face would not stain your brow's gold.


Incense covered your altars, crowned with grain; I dried and swelled Henares with tears and fire.


Today pain and anger force me to see two seas in one stream when I behold my eyes.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: A Thousand Times I Keep Silent, Though I Long to Break
translations.text:
A thousand times I keep silent, though longing to split heaven with cries, and try to give my tongue voice, seeing it lie in deathly silence;


thought runs in my soul like a courier, loud and tearful from pain, a new Orpheus in death's shadow.


Memory or hope finds no sweet image by which will may live secure:


all in me is curse, delayed death, inconsolable weeping, Heaven's disdain, fortune's error.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To a Judge Who Is Merchandise
translations.text:
The laws by which you judge, Batinus, you study less than sell; you understand what is bought; the Fleece pleases you more than Jason.


Interpreting human and divine law, you offend them, and as you shrink or stretch it, your hand prepares the verdict.


You cannot hear cheap pleas; only payment dispels doubts; bargains govern you, not texts.


Since intent and interest do not change, wash hands with Pilate or hang with Judas by your purse.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To a Beautiful Cross-Eyed Lady
translations.text:
If your eyes looked only one way, what would they not burn? If not in different directions, sunset or East would freeze.


The crooked leftward glance is criminal; your lights fire wicked, sweet, burning light with deceitful aim.


They see what they do not look at; all who see them are spoils; conquest gives soul rewards and torments.


What law moved the bad jurist, when both eyes are monarchs, to call them viscounts of sight?
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Condolences to Her Husband
translations.text:
Let she who was your eyes' light now turn grief to water, illustrious duke, whose tears every feeling mortal shares.


Your dove fled your nest and makes hers in dawn's arms; she treads and enchants stars, clothed in the new sun.


Weep, for weeping is consolation; let sighs accompanying her in sacrifice not cease.


Weep until you see her; since Heaven took her from envy, pity will compel it to return her.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: What Lonelier Bird Was Ever Seen beneath a Roof?
translations.text:
What lonelier bird was seen beneath a roof, or beast on mountain? I am deserted by myself, for you left my soul dissolved in tears.


I shall always weep my greatest good; every morsel is pain and gall; night anguish, rest anxiety, bed battlefield.


Sleep, death's image, surpasses death in cruelty, preventing the supreme good of seeing you.


So great your grace and beauty that, since Nature made you, Nature can perform a miracle.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Sonnet to Death
translations.text:
Help, in King Jesus' name! The church cannot save the wretch, for his killer entered holy ground, fearing neither royal house nor sacred place.


Help justice, bring lights, chase him, seize the culprit; he waits cloaked for the watch.


They seized him because his sword exceeded regulation; but seeing it bloody,


justice asked who he was. He uncovered: I am Death. Are you Death? Go on in peace.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Now, O Minister, Fix Your Care
translations.text:
O minister, take care not to wrong the wretched or strong; when taking gold and silver, remember you leave polished steel.


You leave sword and lance to the unfortunate, and power and reason to defeat you: starving people do not fear death.


Who sees certain ruin hates its cause more than ruin, and this enrages him.


He loves nakedness and grievance with despair when his oppressor offers vengeance.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: On the Brevity of Life
translations.text:
How you slip between my hands! How you glide away, my age! What silent steps, cold death, making all equal!


Fierce, you scale youth's weak earthen wall; my heart awaits the final day's flight without seeing wings.


O mortal condition, harsh fate! I cannot wish to live tomorrow without procuring death!


Each instant is a new execution warning how fragile, wretched, vain life is.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To Daphne, Fleeing Apollo
translations.text:
“An alchemist called Sun runs after you, Daphne—and are you so cruel? You turn bat, fleeing Sun and light.


“He wants you if he catches you in this rough wood; quiver rattles, purse is mute, dog dies.


“Peddler of signs and planets, he gestures, loaded with blushes and comets.”


I told her; she grafted herself into laurel bark, and Sun remained pickled in darkness.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Let Me Cry Aloud the Good I Lose
translations.text:
Let me cry aloud the good I lose, if weeping moves pity; let me act mad, for I am a poor lover sane.


Net, prison, and tyrant severity are too little to show pain if I remember what I was.


Let all hear: weary of waiting, since I lived without foresight, let me die without judgment.


Let me sate myself shouting. Let this beast know I could die but not change.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: How You Slip Away between My Hands!...
translations.text:
How you slip between my hands! How you glide away, my age! What silent steps, cold death, making all equal!


Fierce, you scale youth's weak earthen wall; my heart awaits the final day's flight without seeing wings.


O mortal condition, harsh fate! I cannot wish to live tomorrow without procuring death!


Each instant is a new execution warning how fragile, wretched, vain life is.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Curly Locks, Lawlessly Unbound...
translations.text:
Curly locks, lawlessly unbound, Midas once held; black stars kindled in snow.


Roses anticipating spring, defended from time; dawns rising in laughter, guarded by carnation.


Living planets of heaven, through which Lisi rules freedoms bound in their lights.


She is a rational sphere lighting earth, where Love reigns over all she sees and lives in all she kills.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: As the Farmer Fears Rain with Thunder, So Is His Shepherdess's Gaze
translations.text:
You saw dry fields accuse clouds and rain; then furrows fear watering threatening lightning.


They prefer dryness to burning, seeing fire accompany water, lightning, and thunder.


So my eyes fear beauty coveted in yours, longing for pure light.


As they opened, they struck lightning and set aflame in me all they saw.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To an Ugly Woman Afraid of Mice
translations.text:
What the mouse should do seeing you, you do seeing it, fleeing and screaming, though you are a mousetrap in cleanliness and traps.


Who saw you flee would judge you aged cheese, for wrinkles make you look like cheese.


Who thought mice eat the white poison heaped on your face?


Why leap walls fleeing, when mice will not gnaw your dirty wool complexion?
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Comparing Two Jealous Bulls, He Asks Lisi Not to Wonder at His Jealousy
translations.text:
See ground rise and day shorten with dust from bloody combat, in bulls' jealous courage driven by love?


See blood, smoke from black brow, and stubborn struggle the loving heart displays?


Then why, Lisi, marvel that when love dries my veins a volcano bursts in rage?


Can bulls feel fury, while you forbid me to deafen mountains with weeping?
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: A Lover Grateful for a Dream's Lying Flattery
translations.text:
Ah, Floralva! I dreamed that you... shall I say? Yes: I enjoyed you. Who but a dreaming lover joins hell to heaven?


Love mingled my flames with your snow and ice, like opposing arrows, chastely.


I said: may I never sleep if awake, and if asleep never wake.


But I woke, and saw I lived with death and with life was dead.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: If You Are a God, Love, What Is Your Heaven?...
translations.text:
If god, Love, what heaven? If lord, what estates? Where servants and seat?


If mortal veil disguises you, what retreats? If rich, where goods? Why naked in sun and ice?


Painting you winged and blindfolded means painter and world mock you.


So do I, since Lisis's honest face cowed you until you look like blindman's buff.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To a Fountain Where Lisida Came to See Herself
translations.text:
Laughing pure fountain—you learn from my eyes to be a river, rushing from eyes sending tears—


if cold traps you in crystal, my tears for Lisida burn you; your flood is mine.


You hoard her image; I lavish tears on your currents, soul and faith on Lisida.


I judged seas bitter and cruel, but not fountains' clear, laughing, sweet water.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.
